findings.title: Guard bypassed by rename in same update request
findings.problem: transfer_setting checks _is_subsystem_managed(setting.alias) on the row as loaded inside the transaction. Both PUT /v1/settings/project/{id} and PUT /v1/settings/user/{id} run SettingsService.update_settings (which applies the new alias) before transfer_setting, so a request that renames a subsystem-managed row (__internal__, codemie:project:, Schedule_, budget-tracking alias) to a non-reserved alias while changing project_name sees only the new alias and the row is moved anyway.
findings.impact: The ticket's rule (managed rows must not move via the one-row transfer) can be evaded with a single request by a caller who may write the row; the managed row ends up in another project under an ordinary alias. Exploit requires a rename combined with a project change, and write access to the row; reachability of the PUT paths confirmed from the routers.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate _is_subsystem_managed on the pre-update alias: in both PUT routers check existing_setting.alias before update_settings when project_changed (or reject reserved-row edits in update_settings), keeping the guard in transfer_setting too. Add a regression test renaming a managed row while changing project_name.
